item.title: Sustainable Luxury Tourism: Opportunities, Tensions, and Impacts
item.content:encoded:
Kalliopi Chatzipanagiotou, University of Glasgow

Achilleas Boukis, University of Birmingham

George Christodoulides, American University of Sharjah

Raffaele Filieri, Audencia Business School

Luxury tourism is growing rapidly, yet research has largely focused on economic dimensions while neglecting broader sustainability, social, and ethical implications. A fundamental tension exists between luxury's exclusivity and the responsible resource use required for sustainability. While many luxury tourists express concern for sustainability, limited empirical evidence shows how these concerns translate into actual behavior or what trade-offs they accept.

The experiences of local communities and workers remain largely overlooked, revealing gaps regarding social inequality and regenerative development. Luxury tourism can amplify inequalities by concentrating wealth in exclusive areas while burdening local communities, ecosystems, and workers. Additionally, technological innovations like artificial intelligence and virtual reality are transforming luxury tourism production and consumption, raising questions about authenticity, cultural representation, and digital exclusion.

Appel publié par Journal of Sustainable Tourism. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
